# Ukrainian {#sec-ukrainian}

*Отче наш.* Ukrainian received the prayer through Church Slavonic rather than
Latin, which is why this chapter sits apart from the western vernaculars
before it: its ancestor is the [Ancient Greek](ancient-greek.qmd) of the
Byzantine liturgy, carried north in the tenth century and translated into the
Slavonic used across the Orthodox world for the next six hundred years.

The transliteration under each line romanises the **sound**, as
[Modern Greek](modern-greek.qmd) does, not the spelling.

::: {.pdf-keep}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Pronunciation key

| Letter | Here | Sounds like |
|---|---|---|
| г | `h` | *h*ouse — **not** a hard *g* |
| ґ | `g` | *g*o (rare, a separate letter) |
| х | `kh` | Scottish lo*ch* |
| и | `y` | b*i*t, further back |
| і | `i` | mach*i*ne |
| ї | `yi` | *ye*ast |
| є | `ye` | *ye*s |
| ц | `ts` | ca*ts* |
| ч, ш | `ch`, `sh` | — |
| щ | `shch` | fre*sh ch*eese |
| ь | `'` | softens the consonant before it |
| ’ | `'` | the apostrophe: keeps the consonant hard |

The letter to watch is **г**. In Ukrainian it is a breathy *h*, not the *g* of
Russian, so *лукавого* ends "-*voho*" and *сьогодні* begins "*s'oho-*". It is
the single loudest marker of the language, and getting it wrong is the
commonest mistake a reader coming from Russian makes.
:::
:::

## Liturgical text

The form prayed today, with the doxology attached.

::: {.prayer lang="uk" speech="uk-UA" #uk-liturgical}
| Отче наш, що єси на небесах!
| [Otche nash, shcho yesy na nebesakh!]{.tr}
| Нехай святиться ім'я Твоє,
| [Nekhay svyatytsya im'ya Tvoye,]{.tr}
| нехай прийде Царство Твоє,
| [nekhay pryyde Tsarstvo Tvoye,]{.tr}
| нехай буде воля Твоя,
| [nekhay bude volya Tvoya,]{.tr}
| як на небі, так і на землі.
| [yak na nebi, tak i na zemli.]{.tr}
| Хліб наш насущний дай нам сьогодні.
| [Khlib nash nasushchnyy day nam s'ohodni.]{.tr}
| І прости нам провини наші, як і ми прощаємо винуватцям нашим.
| [I prosty nam provyny nashi, yak i my proshchayemo vynuvatsyam nashym.]{.tr}
| І не введи нас у спокусу, але визволи нас від лукавого.
| [I ne vvedy nas u spokusu, ale vyzvoly nas vid lukavoho.]{.tr}
| Бо Твоє є царство, і сила, і слава навіки. Амінь.
| [Bo Tvoye ye tsarstvo, i syla, i slava naviky. Amin'.]{.tr}
:::

Unlike the Latin tradition, the doxology is not detachable here. Byzantine
practice has always joined *Бо Твоє є царство* to the prayer, which is why
the Orthodox and Greek Catholic text carries it and the
[Latin](latin.qmd) one never does.

## Ohiyenko's Matthew

Ivan Ohiyenko's translation of the Bible, the standard Ukrainian Protestant
and academic text, differs in two places that this book has been following
across languages.

::: {.prayer lang="uk" speech="uk-UA" #uk-ohiyenko .variant}
| Отче наш, що єси на небесах!
| [Otche nash, shcho yesy na nebesakh!]{.tr}
| Нехай святиться Ім'я Твоє,
| [Nekhay svyatytsya Im'ya Tvoye,]{.tr}
| нехай прийде Царство Твоє, нехай буде воля Твоя,
| [nekhay pryyde Tsarstvo Tvoye, nekhay bude volya Tvoya,]{.tr}
| як на небі, так і на землі.
| [yak na nebi, tak i na zemli.]{.tr}
| Хліба нашого насущного дай нам сьогодні.
| [Khliba nashoho nasushchnoho day nam s'ohodni.]{.tr}
| І прости нам борги наші, як і ми прощаємо винуватцям нашим.
| [I prosty nam borhy nashi, yak i my proshchayemo vynuvatsyam nashym.]{.tr}
| І не введи нас у випробовування, але визволи нас від лукавого.
| [I ne vvedy nas u vyprobovuvannya, ale vyzvoly nas vid lukavoho.]{.tr}
| Бо Твоє є царство, і сила, і слава навіки. Амінь.
| [Bo Tvoye ye tsarstvo, i syla, i slava naviky. Amin'.]{.tr}
:::

**борги, not провини.** Ohiyenko keeps the debt of the Greek *ὀφειλήματα*
where the liturgical text has *провини*, faults. This is the same split that
sent [Spanish](spanish.qmd) to *ofensas* and [English](english.qmd) to
*trespasses*, while [German](german.qmd) escaped it because *Schuld* means
both at once.

**випробовування, not спокуса.** "Testing" rather than "temptation" — the
sixth petition again, answered a third way. [Italian](italian.qmd) changed
the verb, [Lithuanian](lithuanian.qmd) and [Modern Greek](modern-greek.qmd)
changed what is asked of God, and Ohiyenko changed the noun: not enticement to
sin but trial, which is where the [ELLC English](english.qmd) *time of trial*
also lands.

## Before Ukrainian

The oldest printed ancestor of this text in the East Slavonic world is the
Ostroh Bible of 1581, in Church Slavonic:

> Ѿче на́шъ иже еси на н[е]б[е]сѣ[хъ], да с[вѧ]ти́тсѧ и́мѧ Твое́ …

Six hundred years of liturgy stand between that line and the one at the top of
this chapter, and yet *да святиться* and *нехай святиться* are recognisably
the same request. The square brackets are the modern editors' — the original
abbreviates the sacred words under a *titlo*, a stroke drawn over the letters.
